doc.title: Phil Schaap interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003

title: Chick Webb paper and teaching at Columbia
summary: His Chick Webb paper led to trouble for his teacher; Columbia's history department hired him to lecture on jazz.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: That’s great. When did you have an opportunity to do some writing in liner notes and all those kinds of things?

Well I wrote some papers on jazz in college and I wrote one in high school. That’s why I left the major music program in the New York City public school system. He actually thought I could play trumpet, he was wrong. I believe his name was Ralph Stein, he was my music teacher at Jamaica High School and he let me do my paper on Chick Webb in my sophomore year of high school. And I did a good job and he gave me a good grade. And then he got in trouble and I said let me out of here.
Because of the subject matter he let you do?

Yes. They didn’t blame me, they could have, he got in trouble. And I said that’s it. Let me out of here. I’ll never take another music course in the school system. And that probably plants the seed of preventing me from overcoming my inferiority, which was for the best, but I was doing off on my own, and I guess I would be fifteen, and intentionally curtailing the music program in the New York City public school system for a righteous, accurate and correct reason. I was mad as hell. Still am obviously.
Because they wanted you to do Bach or Beethoven or somebody like that?

Yeah it was inappropriate. The teacher had approved the topic so it was him who got into trouble, not me, the grade stood. But I said I’ll never take another music course. And that was besides — two more years, two and a half. And I never did. And I was mad. And they wouldn’t let me talk about Duke Ellington in the classroom either. That continued at Columbia. So I said later for the music major at Columbia, the American history department was hiring me to teach jazz in their American history seminars. I said oh okay. I’m switching. And that’s what I did. That’s when my teaching career started.
Oh. So the music department didn’t want to know about it but the history department recognized it.
